case_name: National Federation of the Blind v. Target Corporation
court: U.S. District Court, Northern District of California
claim_type: Target.com inaccessible to blind users; no alt text, no keyboard navigation
outcome: Class action settlement — $6 million in damages to class members; $3,738,864.96 in attorney fees and costs
estimated_defense_cost: Defense costs plus $3.74M attorney fee award; total exposure exceeded $10M

sources.name: National Federation of the Blind — Official settlement announcement
Wikipedia — National Federation of the Blind v. Target Corp.
W3C WAI — Target Corporation Case Study
SitePoint — Target Settles Accessibility Lawsuit for $6 Million

summary_one_line: First major e-commerce ADA settlement in U.S. history; established that commercial websites are covered by ADA and class-action exposure is real — Target paid $6M+ in 2008.
notes: Court certified the class action in 2007 (first such certification for website ADA case). Settlement approved August 2008. NFB monitored compliance via quarterly and annual user accessibility tests. Plaintiff Bruce Sexton filed on behalf of all similarly situated blind California residents.
